statement: For a finite simple triangle-free graph $G$, let $m=e(G)$, let $\lambda(G)$ be its adjacency spectral radius, and let $D(G)=\min_{A\cap B=\varnothing}|E(G)\mathbin{\triangle}E(K_{A,B})|$, where $A,B\subseteq V(G)$ and vertices outside $A\cup B$ are isolated in the target; empty parts are allowed. Does an absolute constant $C<\infty$ exist such that $D(G)\le C(m-\lambda(G)^2)$ for every such $G$?

source.reference: Full readings reading-spectral-book-full-v1 (arXiv:2609.20225v2, Lemmas 4.3-4.4 and Theorem 1.9) and reading-edge-spectral-full-v1 (arXiv:2508.15271v2, Theorem 4.1).

observation: This asks whether qualitative edge-spectral stability admits any uniform linear modulus, independently of the sharp coefficient. The same two full readings supply the established comparison. It has a broader possible positive answer but does not distinguish the coefficient suggested by the bipartite theorem and five-cycle.
notes: Exploration does not establish openness or proof credit. The exact statement must receive a bounded native attempt and current literature review.
